q: Are galvanised, colour-coated and tinplate sheets under CN 7210 covered by CBAM?
title: CBAM CN 7210: GI, PPGI and tinplate
short: Yes. Coated flat steel 600 mm or wider, CN 7210, covers tinplate, galvanised (GI, GL) and painted sheet (PPGI), and is covered under the Chapter 72 line. Direct emissions only. The zinc and paint are not CBAM precursors; the steel substrate is.
audience: Indian GI, GL, PPGI and tinplate exporters to the EU

p: Yes. CN 7210 is flat-rolled iron or non-alloy steel, 600 mm or wider, clad, plated or coated. Narrower coated strip falls under 7212, also covered. Coated alloy and stainless sheet falls under 7225 and 7219.

ul: The cold-rolled or hot-rolled substrate coil. A bought coil needs its maker's embedded emissions per tonne.
Zinc, aluminium-zinc, tin and paint are not covered precursors and do not need a figure.

p: The Commission sets default values by CN code and country of origin in the annex to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621, with a mark-up that rises over the first years. We do not quote the figure here. Open the annex, find your code and India, and treat it as the number your buyer pays on if you send nothing usable.

sections.h: What to send your EU importer
ul: Direct embedded emissions per tonne of coated sheet, in tonnes of CO2, for the period the importer asks about.
The production route and the installation's name, location and, if registered, its CBAM registry ID.
Each precursor's embedded emissions and quantity per tonne, and who made it if you bought it.
Whether a verifier accredited for CBAM has checked the figure. The importer can only use actual values that are verified.

p: Counting the coating's weight as steel. Declare per tonne of the coated product shipped, but report the substrate's embedded emissions scaled to the steel actually used, plus the direct fuel of your galvanising or paint line furnaces.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and purchase invoices into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for. It does not file CBAM declarations or verify emissions.
